notable_absence.finding: The current-generation search:create-search-index-ui.md states 'Your user account has the Search Admin role for the bucket where you want to create the index' (a concrete requiresServerRole -> role:fts-admin relation). This old-generation page only gestures at the requirement in the vaguest terms - 'you must have permission to log into the console, create indexes, and perform searches. For information on Role-Based Access Control, see Authorization' - and names no specific role, and 'Authorization' is not even rendered as a link in the Markdown snapshot. No requiresServerRole relation can be extracted from this page with real evidence; the concrete role name is a fact this page simply lacks, not one this extraction is choosing to omit.

cross_component_finding: The page's failover note - 'If one or more of the nodes in the cluster running data service goes down and/or are failed over, indexing progress may show a value > 100%' - ties Search index build progress directly to Data service node failover behavior, but the page never names a failover or high-availability concept, and the registry has no standalone failover concept id to attach this to (only vbucket-level ones). Recorded here rather than forced onto an ill-fitting predicate.
cross_product_finding: This exact filename is not among the round's 14 pages with a confirmed 7.2 twin, but its content is clearly the OLD-generation duplicate of search/create-search-index-ui.md's task: the same Add Index walkthrough against the travel-sample bucket, using the Couchbase Web Console's Search tab. Two of this page's sibling pages in this same batch (fts-creating-index-specifying-advanced-settings.md, fts-creating-index-using-the-index-definition-preview.md) cover the standard editor's Advanced panel and Definition Preview panel respectively - together the three pages document one classic-editor task across sub-pages, each mapping onto an existing search: concept rather than needing a new shared task id.
